answer: Zero-knowledge passport attestation deters Sybil attacks when agents trade willow baskets, linen thread, or lantern goods by tying each key to a physical ID. At signup, an agent submits a ZK-SNARK proving its key binds to a state-signed NFC passport with a deterministic nullifier a ledger deduplicates. Because one document yields one nullifier per epoch, attackers incur the cost of acquiring a separate ID per clone. Still, corrupt issuers or identity brokers can supply excess documents.
